authority: #K2-450 sec.2.5: before the authorised N=1 the ENG must file the sec.16.3 four-element artifact and answer the sec.13 sentence.
element1_one_line_death_cause: the engine allocates channels PER NET IN SEQUENCE, so each net takes its own span and the spans overlap; whoever is served last finds no slot and is starved - which is exactly the observed residual rotation (P3V3 closed -> PWR_BTN_OUT broke -> I2C2_SCL broke).
element2_proven_facts: R1394 conservation count: frame 1286.2 mm^2, pitch 0.40 mm, 4 signal layers => CAPACITY = 12862 track-mm (geometric upper bound) vs DEMAND = 257.3 track-mm (sum of 14 in-frame nets' MST lower bounds) => a ~50x margin => the frame is NOT area-limited.
Therefore R1392's (B) infeasibility certificate is VOID (refuted by #K2-450 sec.2.2) and (A) feasibility holds at both levels: the drawing applies 98/0 with a clean DRC, and the demand is affordable.

Residual rotation over three runs: R1362 {I2C1_SDA, P3V3} -> R1372 {I2C1_SDA, PWR_BTN_OUT} -> R1392 {I2C1_SDA, I2C2_SCL}; each targeted fix closed its net (P3V3 by the bridge+D2 tie; PWR_BTN_OUT by freeing its dR port) and another net broke => the allocator, not the geometry, is binding.
The drawing is complete and anchored: 98 pieces, anchor audit ok=True padless=0, stitched-field DRC {unconnected_items: 343} with zero shorts/crossings/clearance.
The kernel of the new means exists and is regression-proven (test_C450): sequential() overlaps and starves; joint() packs disjointly and serves all; a too-small span is named.

element3_corrected_complete_plan.status: DRAWING determinate; the JOINT ALLOCATION is specified but NOT YET WIRED (honest: wiring is the remaining generator change).
element3_corrected_complete_plan.per_line_drawing: the 98 frozen pieces already on the board: NRST dR port; P3V3_AUX plane ties (C90.1, B.Cu fragment incl. the R1.2 pad anchor, In5 fragment); I2C1 group corridor (SCL lane; SDA lane + joint + the E2.5 pad-anchored segment); P3V3 (anchored In4 bridge at y=35.5, declared outside_dR) + the D2.1 tie. Each piece is a frozen constant (layer + endpoints), i.e. determinate.
element3_corrected_complete_plan.joint_allocation_to_be_wired: replace the maze's per-net sequential assignment with ONE pass that (a) collects the in-frame nets' required spans along the corridor axis, (b) packs them disjointly with the pitch (0.20 width + 0.20 clearance = 0.40 mm) via k2_joint_channel_alloc_v1.joint(), (c) hands the whole channel map to the maze in ONE batch (the maze then routes INSIDE its own corridor, and cannot take a slot that another net holds).
element3_corrected_complete_plan.per_corridor_conservation: CAPACITY per corridor axis = (corridor length / pitch); DEMAND = the number of nets that must cross it. For the frame as a whole: capacity 12862 mm vs demand 257 mm (50x). Per-corridor numbers must be read from the actual channel map once wired (NOT domain-level padding).
element3_corrected_complete_plan.buildability_answer_sec13: Can a construction crew wire straight from this drawing? YES for the drawing itself - every piece is a frozen constant and the anchor audit is green. The OUTSTANDING question is not 'can it be drawn' but 'is the allocation computed jointly': with the joint allocation wired, each net owns a corridor and the crew (the maze) merely follows it; without it, the maze competes and starves someone.
element3_corrected_complete_plan.explicit_honesty: element 3 is therefore NOT yet fully closed: the drawing half is determinate; the allocation half is specified + kernel-proven but NOT wired.

element4_buildability.detail: the only outside-dR item is the P3V3 bridge (declared, with conservation): same-net plane addition => capacity grows, demand unchanged. Everything else is no_move.

blocking_item: WIRING the joint allocator into the chain (a generator change) remains. Per #K2-450 sec.2.5 the N=1 must not be run before it, so the run stays deferred.
